thesis: NRG is a vertically integrated independent power producer and home-services company that pairs ~25 GW of dispatchable generation (mostly natural gas) with one of the largest competitive retail electricity books in the U.S. plus the Vivint Smart Home platform. The January 2026 close of the ~$12B LS Power acquisition (18 gas plants, ~13 GW, plus the CPower commercial and industrial virtual power plant) doubled generation capacity and drove Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA up 34% YoY to $1.217B, with 2026 guidance of ~$5.575B adjusted EBITDA, ~$8.90 adjusted EPS and ~$3.05B free cash flow before growth. The stock has nevertheless fallen ~41% over the past year to a fresh 52-week low, because the deal was debt-funded (total debt $23.5B and cash of only $162M at 30 Jun 2026), two consecutive quarters missed adjusted EPS on higher interest expense, and Texas Governor Abbott's data center permit freeze - expanded on 21 Sep 2026 to a TCEQ permit halt pending ERCOT and water audits - has cast doubt on the ERCOT load-growth thesis. At ~7.8x EV on guided 2026 EBITDA and a ~15% forward FCF-before-growth yield against a $189-198 analyst consensus target, the risk/reward is attractive but the leverage and Texas regulatory overhang make it speculative.

financials.gross_margin: ~10% (TTM EBITDA margin; IPP reporting has no gross profit line)

drivers: Texas lifts the TCEQ data center permit freeze after the ERCOT and Texas Water Development Board audits clear, restoring the ERCOT load-growth narrative that drove the 2025 re-rating

The 1.2 GW / $3.2B Bring Your Own Power combined-cycle plant in Texas converts to a signed 15-year hyperscaler contract, validating ~$500M of annual adjusted EBITDA and ~$375M of annual FCF before growth from late 2029
LS Power synergies and PJM capacity value step-ups push 2027 adjusted EBITDA above the $5.575B 2026 guide, compounding through the contracted development pipeline
Free cash flow before growth of ~$3.05B funds ~$1B of annual debt repayment plus $1.4B+ of buybacks and dividends, pulling leverage back toward 3.0x and compressing the credit-risk discount
The stock re-rates toward the ~$189–198 analyst consensus target as the AI-power trade recovers and NRG closes its EV/EBITDA discount to Vistra and Constellation

base_case.assumptions: NRG delivers 2026 adjusted EBITDA near but slightly below the $5.575B guidance midpoint (management has said results are tracking below the midpoint), converts it to ~$3.0B of FCF before growth, and keeps the ~$1B debt repayment plus $1.4B shareholder-return plan intact. The Texas permit freeze delays but does not cancel ERCOT data center load, and the BYOP contract is signed with late-2029 commercial operation. Multiple recovers from ~7.8x toward 8.5–9x EV/guided EBITDA — roughly 10–12x the ~$8.90–10.50 adjusted EPS band — which lands well short of the analyst consensus but well above the current 52-week low.

risks: The Texas permit halt hardens into a durable moratorium or the legislature strips data center incentives, removing the demand growth that underwrites both the BYOP plant and ERCOT forward power prices — BloombergNEF puts 49.8 GW of Texas data center load at risk of delay
Leverage bites: $23.5B of total debt, debt/equity of 5.17x and TTM interest expense of $1.025B (up from $741M in FY2025) force NRG to choose between deleveraging and shareholder returns
The hyperscaler walks from the 1.2 GW deal or the $3.2B build overruns, leaving NRG with an uncontracted merchant plant and a leverage target already pushed from 2028 to 2029
A third consecutive adjusted EPS miss or a 2026 guidance cut at the 5 Nov 2026 print breaks confidence in the LS Power integration story
Mild weather, collapsing natural gas prices or PJM capacity price mean reversion compress merchant spark spreads, while retail churn erodes the customer book that funds the hedge

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 earnings — the key test of whether 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance of ~$5.575B and adjusted EPS of ~$8.90 hold after two consecutive adjusted EPS misses

Definitive contract signing for the 1.2 GW / $3.2B Bring Your Own Power combined-cycle plant in Texas with a global cloud and AI hyperscaler (15-year term, ~$500M annual adjusted EBITDA, late-2029 commercial operation)

Completion of the ERCOT and Texas Water Development Board audits of ~250–300 interconnection-queue projects and the lifting of Governor Abbott's 21 Sep 2026 TCEQ data center permit halt — no completion date has been announced
Commercial operation of the ~415 MW Texas gas plant backed by the Texas Energy Fund, the first increment of the in-ERCOT brownfield development pipeline
FY2026 results and first formal 2027 guidance, including a full year of LS Power asset ownership versus ~11 months in 2026
Deleveraging milestones toward the 3.0x net leverage target, pushed back from 2028 to 2029 by the BYOP capex commitment

key_risks: Texas regulatory risk — Governor Abbott's TCEQ data center permit halt (21 Sep 2026) and the ERCOT interconnection audit directly threaten the ERCOT load-growth thesis; BloombergNEF estimates 49.8 GW of Texas data center load faces delay
Leverage — $23.5B total debt, $162M cash and debt/equity of 5.17x at 30 Jun 2026 after the ~$12B LS Power acquisition; the 3.0x leverage target slipped from 2028 to 2029
Rising interest expense — TTM interest expense of $1.025B versus $741M in FY2025 was the primary driver of the Q2 2026 adjusted EPS miss
Execution and integration risk on 18 acquired gas facilities plus the CPower virtual power plant platform, alongside $3.2B of new-build capex
Counterparty concentration — a single unnamed hyperscaler underwrites the 1.2 GW BYOP project's economics
Weather and commodity exposure — mild Texas weather already hurt Q1 2026; gas and power price volatility plus PJM capacity price mean reversion can compress merchant margins
Retail competition and customer churn in ERCOT and the East, and Vivint Smart Home subscriber economics
Thin GAAP earnings cover — TTM GAAP EPS of $3.87 against a $1.90 dividend leaves the payout dependent on non-GAAP free cash flow before growth
